chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who drinks wine after Allah, Exalted and Mighty, has prohibited it upon my tongue, is not deserving of being married to when he proposes, nor is he to be interceded for when intercession is made, nor is he to be believed when he narrates, nor is he to be trusted with an entrustment. So whoever trusts him after having knowledge of him in this regard, there is no guarantee for the one who trusted him with Allah, Exalted and Mighty, nor is there any reward for him, nor a compensation.'

key_terms.يُزَوَّجَ: To be married to (in the context of a suitor)

ai.seo_question: What are the social and spiritual consequences of drinking wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith to establish the jurisprudential principle of 'fusuq' (moral depravity) in wine drinkers, rendering them unfit for social and religious roles. The Prophet’s declaration that trust in them carries no divine guarantee ('ضمان') highlights the loss of spiritual merit in transactions with them, a key concept in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of their testimony and intercession.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid Bin Jareer, from Abu Al Rabie Al Shamy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who drinks the wine after Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic having Prohibited it upon my<sup>saww</sup> tongue, so he is not deserving of being married to when he proposes, nor for him to be interceded for when there is intercession, nor should he be ratified when he narrates, nor relied upon an entrustment. So the one who relies upon him after having his knowledge with regards to it, so it is not for those who rely upon him, any guarantee (of security) upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, nor would there be any Rewards for him, nor a compensation’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from Khalid ibn Jarir from abu al-Rabi’ al-Shamiy who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘If one drinks wine after Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has made it unlawful through my tongue, he does not deserve to receive acceptance to his marriage proposal. His intercession is not accepted. He is not considered truthful when speaking and is not trusted about a trust. If one trusts him after knowing his condition, he has no guarantee from Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, or reward or replacement and compensation.’”
